name: JAOCC Shading
definition: A voxel shading algorithm that computes ambient occlusion by counting non-empty neighbors in a cubic neighborhood, applying a depth-weighted dimming factor to the voxel's RGB color. It is noted as slow and having errors with thin objects, but produces smooth results for higher neighbor counts.
summary: JAOCC Shading is a voxel-based ambient occlusion technique that computes depth-weighted dimming by counting non-empty neighbors, avoiding hard lighting transitions at voxel boundaries by using local density instead of explicit surface normals.
